purpose: ASVS V7.5.3 requires further authentication before highly sensitive operations. The existing record said the fund-release path asks for nothing beyond an already-authenticated session. Measurement against the current tree shows that is no longer true: release carries SettlementFinancialMfaGuard, as do seven other money-mutating routes. What was missing was not the control but any check that it stays attached.
stackedReason: Continues the V7.5.x contour and inherits the shared fresh-MFA control from the two branches below it; its scope lists the cumulative diff because the guard measures a branch against main.
requiredInvariants: No runtime behaviour changes on this branch. The settlement controller, its guard and every route are read, never edited; this pass adds a registry, a checker and a corrected record.

The stale record is corrected openly rather than quietly overwritten. It claimed no step-up existed on the command path; eight of nine mutating money routes carry one, and the count is cross-checked against an independent grep.

The one exempt route carries a reason, not silence. bank-callback is @Public() with no user session at all - authenticity comes from a signature binding partner, key version, event id and the canonical body fingerprint - so there is nobody to re-authenticate.
A surface that declares no step-up marker is refused rather than passing trivially, and an exemption without a reason, for a missing route, or for a route already guarded each fail.

What this scanner cannot see is written down instead of implied absent: membership commands and registration decisions are gated in services, not decorators, and are proven by their own behavioural tests.

No dependency, schema, migration, RLS or policy change. No registration business logic, 1C, marketing or presentation code. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: Measured: 9 mutating routes on the settlement controller, 8 carrying the step-up, 1 exempt with a stated reason. Both numbers agree with an independent grep.

The controller parser was WRONG in its first version and the error is recorded: walking line by line, it reset its accumulator on any line not starting with @, and a multi-line @RateLimit({...}) consists of such lines - so it lost three routes of nine, including deal/:id/release, the most sensitive one. It now splits the class on member boundaries, and a test pins the route count against grep.

Three mutations of the tree each turn the checker red: removing the guard from fund release (named by exact route), making the guard stop failing closed on an absent user, and breaking the member split.

V7.5.3 PASS is machine-revocable: four mutations with the matrix rebuilt each time - unguarding fund release, untracking the registry, disabling the route check, and hiding the service-layer note - all four drive the verdict to NOT_ASSESSED.

Two of the decision's own conditions were found too weak by that run and fixed here: the bare guard marker survived unguarding release because seven other routes still carry it, and the serviceLayerStepUps key survived replacing its content with 'n/a'. Both now bind the content they are about.
Matrix on this head: PASS 129 -> 132, FAIL 90 -> 87 across the stack. scripts/security 153/153 green.
